newsitem.title: USA: One-man U.S. Senate hearing ends in New Orleans.
newsitem.headline: One-man U.S. Senate hearing ends in New Orleans.

text.p: Senate Rules Committee Chairman John Warner said Thursday that his committee has not unearthed information that would overturn Democratic Sen. Mary Landrieu's 5,788-vote victory last fall.

"We have not, thus far, in my judgment, seen evidence that would overturn the election," Warner said after a two-day closed-door hearing on defeated Republican Senate candidate Woody Jenkins' controversial challenge to Landrieu's win.

Warner, a Virginia Republican, said he would return to the city in 10 days to review additional financial records of the state's gambling industry's political contributions. The Senate election was on the same ballot with a referendum on legalized gambling. Jenkins has charged that the Louisiana Independent Federation of Electors (LIFE) plotted with gambling interests to throw the election to Landrieu.

Jenkins has also maintained that phantom voters and individuals casting multiple ballots last year, particularly in New Orleans, were widespread and he should be seated or a new election called. Warner has said that a number of election laws were not followed, but not enough to change the outcome.

The investigation has erupted into a bitter partisan political battle between Republicans, led by Warner, and Democrats, who pulled out of the committee probe because they said it had gone on long enough and was without basis.

Warner was the only committee member present to hear testimony from 26 subpoenaed witnesses and to review various financial records, including those of LIFE, a predominantly black political organization created in the '60s when there were no black elected officials in Louisiana, and chaired by New Orleans Mayor Marc Morial, a Democrat.
